system.name: SIL-C
system.one_liner: Framework for skill incremental learning that keeps downstream policies compatible with evolving skills via a bilateral lazy-learning mapping, without policy retraining.

content.variant_note: a two-track phase timeline plus the SIL-C framework box on top, then forward and backward compatibility cases as stacked bands with robot-kitchen renders
content.argues: Skill updates must stay compatible with older (backward) and future (forward) policies; SIL-C does this by mapping policy subtasks to the evolving skill decoder through a lazy learning interface.
content.subject: A policy-skill timeline over four phases, the SIL-C policy-interface-decoder stack, and forward and backward compatibility cases on robot-kitchen renders.

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw a setting that evolves over time as two colour-coded tracks with phase nodes and version labels, then give each property to be shown its own coloured band that repeats the same chain and ends in a bold one-sentence definition; thumbnail copies of the timeline in the band headers tie each case back to it.
lessons.suits: Continual, incremental or versioned learning papers where several compatibility or consistency properties are defined over the same sequence of updates and shown on one example task.

evidence: Figure 1 illustrates a policy-compatible SIL scenario involving two types of skill-policy compatibility
which ensures that a newly added skill can be effectively utilized during the training of future downstream policies
ensures that existing downstream policies can continue to use newly added or updated skills without requiring re-training

summary: SIL-C is a framework for skill incremental learning in which downstream policies keep working while the skill library is updated, using a bilateral lazy learning mapping between the subtasks a policy names and the skills a decoder can run. Figure 1 is a tall poster-style figure in three bands. The top band draws a two-track timeline (green Policy track with square nodes, yellow Skill track with circle nodes over Phases 1 to 4, Policy V1 and V2 above, Skill Decoder V1 to V1.3 below) beside the SIL-C stack of Policy, Lazy Learning Interface and Skill Decoder with an agent and environment loop. Below, Forward and Backward Skill Compatibility bands each show a left-to-right chain with robot-kitchen renders, circled step numbers and check marks, and end in a one-sentence definition strip.

notes: The pre-screen order (concept-schematic, side-by-side-contrast) is kept; model-anatomy and worked-walkthrough are added for the SIL-C stack and the numbered kitchen renders. Not explained in the figure or the quoted paragraph: the meaning of the two dark grey nodes on the timeline, of the dimmed renders (read as earlier or not yet adapted states) and of the small timeline copies in the band headers (read as locators). The flame belongs to a stove burner in the kitchen scene, not to a state marker. The canvas in the digest is smaller than the drawn content, so the preview is the reference for what is shown.
